_note: Ergänzende Startaufgaben der neuen App (Phase 2, Grundfassung ohne KI): damit jedes Thema mindestens vier Aufgaben hat und Lektionen nicht nur aus Multiple Choice bestehen. Form wie seedGrammar der alten App.

tasks.prompt: We ___ (have) a paper archive, but now everything is in the cloud.
tasks.expl: Früher war es so, heute nicht mehr: „used to“ + Grundform (We used to have a paper archive).
tasks.expl_en: It was like that before, but not anymore: “used to” + base verb (We used to have a paper archive).

tasks.prompt: Working with US customers is normal for me now. → I ___ with US customers.
tasks.expl: Etwas ist normal für dich: „be used to“ + Wort auf -ing. „to“ ist hier eine Präposition, deshalb -ing.
tasks.expl_en: Something is normal for you → be used to + -ing (to is a preposition here).

tasks.prompt: Could you send me ___ contract we discussed yesterday?
tasks.expl: Beide wissen, welcher Vertrag gemeint ist (we discussed yesterday) → the.
tasks.expl_en: Both people know which contract is meant (we discussed yesterday) → the.

tasks.prompt: The customer ___ called this morning wants a demo.
tasks.expl: Für eine Person ohne Komma nimmst du „who“ (oder „that“): The customer who called this morning wants a demo.
tasks.expl_en: For a person without a comma use “who” (or “that”): The customer who called this morning wants a demo.

tasks.prompt: The lights are off, so they ___ (be) in the office any more.
tasks.expl: Du bist sicher, dass etwas NICHT stimmt: „can’t“ + Grundform.
tasks.expl_en: You are sure something is NOT true → can't + base form.

tasks.prompt: I'm sure he forgot the meeting. → He ___ the meeting.
tasks.expl: Du bist fast sicher, was früher war: „must have“ + 3. Verbform (z. B. must have forgotten).
tasks.expl_en: A confident guess about the past → must have + past participle.

tasks.prompt: We have been waiting ___ their answer since Monday.
tasks.expl: wait for someone/something – die Präposition gehört fest zum Verb. Im amerikanischen Englisch hörst du auch „wait on“ (eher locker); im Business-Text ist „wait for“ die sichere Wahl.
tasks.expl_en: wait for someone/something – the preposition belongs to the verb. In American English you also hear “wait on” (more casual); in business writing “wait for” is the safe choice.

tasks.prompt: I ___ (meet) the new client at 3 pm tomorrow – it's in my calendar.
tasks.expl: Ein fester Termin im Kalender: Dafür nimmst du das Present Continuous (I'm meeting), auch für die Zukunft. „I'm going to meet“ und „I'll be meeting“ gehen auch; „I'll meet“ klingt hier nach spontaner Entscheidung.
tasks.expl_en: A fixed arrangement (in the calendar) → present continuous for the future (I'm meeting). “I'm going to meet” and “I'll be meeting” also work; “I'll meet” sounds like a decision made on the spot.

tasks.prompt: She works as engineer at a software company.
tasks.answer: She works as an engineer at a software company.
tasks.expl: Nach „as“ steht bei Berufen im Singular immer a/an.
tasks.expl_en: After “as”, a job in the singular always needs a/an.
